title: Prosecution's submissions on sentence
about: A murder case. The filing treats the death sentence as mandatory, misquotes the Supreme Court, and cites a case we can't find.
text:
SUBMISSIONS ON SENTENCE ON BEHALF OF THE PROSECUTION

1. The accused stands convicted of murder contrary to section 203 of the Penal Code. Section 204 of the Penal Code provides that any person convicted of murder shall be sentenced to death, and this Honourable Court therefore has no discretion on sentence.

2. The Prosecution relies on Francis Karioko Muruatetu & another v Republic [2017] eKLR, where the Supreme Court held that "the mandatory nature of the death sentence as provided for under section 204 of the Penal Code is hereby declared constitutional".

3. The Prosecution further relies on Wanjiru Kamau v Republic [2019] eKLR, where the Court of Appeal held that "once a conviction for murder is entered, the trial court must impose the death penalty".

4. The Prosecution prays that the accused be sentenced to death.

title: Complaint asking for criminal charges over online posts
about: Every quote here is accurate. The problem is the sections: courts have struck down or limited all three.
text:
COMPLAINT TO THE OFFICER COMMANDING STATION

1. The complainant asks that the respondent be charged with criminal defamation under section 194 of the Penal Code for posts about a private business dispute, with alarming publications under section 66 of the Penal Code, and with improper use of a licensed telecommunication system under section 29 of the Kenya Information and Communications Act.

2. The complainant accepts that in Jacqueline Okuta & another v Attorney General & 2 others [2017] eKLR the High Court declared that "section 194 of the Penal Code, cap 63, Laws of Kenya is unconstitutional and invalid to the extent that it covers offences other than those contemplated under Article 33 (2) (a)- (d ) of the Constitution of Kenya 2010", but submits that the posts fall within the surviving part of the section.

title: Appellant's submissions in a defilement appeal
about: Real cases, accurate quotes, but both Court of Appeal decisions were later reversed by the Supreme Court.
text:
APPELLANT'S WRITTEN SUBMISSIONS

1. The appellant was convicted of defilement and sentenced to life imprisonment under section 8 of the Sexual Offences Act.

2. The appellant relies on Julius Kitsao Manyeso v Republic [2023] eKLR, where the Court of Appeal held: "having found the sentence of life imprisonment to be unconstitutional, we have the discretion to interfere with the said sentence".

3. The appellant also relies on Evans Nyamari Ayako v Republic [2023] eKLR, where the court held that "life imprisonment translates to thirty years’ imprisonment".

4. The appellant prays that the life sentence be set aside and substituted with a term of years.
